summary: This bill directs the Interior Secretary to complete all actions within 365 days so that about 40 acres at the Wounded Knee Massacre site on the Pine Ridge Reservation is held in restricted fee status by the Oglala Sioux and Cheyenne River Sioux Tribes, subject to a tribal covenant barring gaming and most taxation or alienation.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior to complete administrative actions for land transfer but contains no appropriations, funding mechanisms, or spending directives. It has no bearing on government spending levels.

Section 2(1)(D) explicitly states that the Tribal land 'shall not be subject to taxation by a State or local government.' This provides a tax exemption, which constitutes a minor reduction in taxes on the affected land.
The bill concerns tribal land status and has no provisions related to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
No provisions relate to immigration pathways, borders, or enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions involve military or defense spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations or protections.
No provisions relate to welfare programs or social safety net policies.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill assigns civil and criminal jurisdiction to the Oglala Sioux Tribe but does not engage with sentencing reform, policing, or rehabilitation policies.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
